wk.e78842b: How much prices have risen compared with the same month a year earlier. The statistics office reports the value at the start of the following month; so you always steer looking in the rear-view mirror.
wk.c10b57a: What households and firms expect for the coming months, measured by survey and therefore imprecise. It decides how high wages and prices are set; if it is anchored, inflation is easier to bring down (Z3).
wk.5aab496: The rate at which banks borrow from the central bank. It is set by the Monetary Policy Committee, not the president, as long as the bank is independent; you can apply pressure, replace the leadership or change the law.
wk.9a85d54: The policy rate minus expected inflation. It decides whether money is worth saving or borrowing and acts on demand after about half a year (Z1). If it falls below zero, the bank loses credibility.
wk.b7eface: The external value of the lira. It reacts daily to interest rates, inflation and confidence. A weaker lira makes imports dearer, exports and holidays cheaper.
wk.f964aae: As with the dollar. The EU is Türkiye's most important trading partner.
wk.68a7faf: How much economic output has grown compared with the same quarter a year earlier. Published about two months after the end of the quarter.
wk.8ffcc1c: Share of job seekers in the labour force. Follows growth with a delay.
wk.a32e1d4: What the state spends per year beyond its revenue, as a percentage of economic output: the baseline of the budget law, your spending impulse, the cost of your measures and the extra or reduced interest on the debt.
wk.d2da496: All the state's debt relative to economic output. High inflation lowers the ratio because economic output grows faster in nominal terms than the debt.
wk.181a88e: What the state pays in interest each year. Under the 2026 budget law it was about 3.5 % of GDP, roughly one lira in five of tax revenue. The average rate follows market rates only slowly, because debt is refinanced only when it falls due.
wk.3bbfe0f: What investors demand as a premium for the risk that the state does not pay (five-year CDS). It rises with high inflation, high debt and political uncertainty.
wk.9590242: Exports minus imports of goods, services and transfers, as a percentage of economic output. A lasting deficit must be financed by capital inflows or from reserves — the central bank cannot print foreign currency.
wk.b210b29: Reserves excluding swap liabilities: the central bank's powder against a lira storm. If they fall below 25 bn, markets demand a surcharge on the exchange rate and the risk premium; below 10 bn a balance-of-payments crisis looms.
wk.ac5a079: All reserves of the central bank including gold — but a large part is lent out or owed (swaps, banks' reserve requirements). What matters is the net position; the gap stays constant in the model.
